# Playnite themes - reference (monorepo policy)

## Shape

- A theme is an add-on with `"kind": "theme"` in `src/extensions.json`, laid out like a plugin:
  - `src/themes/<Theme>/AGENTS.md` - the theme's notes; shared anatomy is in `src/themes/AGENTS.md`.
  - `src/themes/<Theme>/info/` - `theme.yaml`, `InstallerManifest.yaml`, `danitesler_<key>.yaml`, `icon.png`, `LICENSE-*.txt` for everything bundled (Playnite's Default theme, icon sets).
  - `src/themes/<Theme>/src/` - XAML at Playnite Default-theme paths, plus `tokens.css` and `Constants.template.xaml`.
- Index row: `key`, `name`, `"kind": "theme"`, `dir`, `addonId`, `requiredApiVersion` = the **theme API** version. Scripts derive `src/`, `info/theme.yaml`, output `artifacts/builds/themes/<key>`. Packages are `.pthm`; database `Type` is `ThemeDesktop`/`ThemeFullscreen`.
- Build output is generated (`src/` copied, `Constants.xaml` rendered from template + `tokens.css`, `thememodifier.yaml`, licenses, `theme.yaml`). Edit sources, never `artifacts/builds/`.

## One vocabulary, each theme's own design

Tokens keep the design system's names; XAML keys do not. `tokens.css` holds the system's tokens verbatim. XAML keys are the same in every theme: Playnite's own keys (`scripts/data/playnite-theme-api.json`) plus the shared keys in `scripts/data/theme-keys.json`. The template maps each key to the token that plays its role, so design-system names appear only in `tokens.css` and template placeholders.

```xml
<!-- BAD: design-system key names -->
<SolidColorBrush x:Key="PrimerBgColorDefaultBrush" Color="{{bgColor-default}}" />
<!-- GOOD: shared key, Primer token as its value -->
<SolidColorBrush x:Key="InputBackgroundBrush" Color="{{bgColor-default}}" />
```

**Picking the key for a spot** (a color in a control template), in order:
1. **Playnite palette key** when its role covers the spot and the design uses that key's token there: `TextBrush`/`TextBrushDarker` text, `TextBrushDark` text on accent, `GlyphBrush` accent, `HoverBrush` hover, `ButtonBackgroundBrush` button fill, `NormalBorderBrush` control edge, `CheckBoxCheckMarkBkBrush`, `PopupBackgroundBrush`/`PopupBorderBrush`, `TooltipBackgroundBrush`, `ExpanderBackgroundBrush` cards, `WindowBackgourndBrush`, `WindowPanelSeparatorBrush` dividers, `WarningBrush`. If the design's value for the role differs from what the palette key holds, point the palette key at the design's token (unrestyled views read it too; note it in the theme's AGENTS.md).
2. **Shared general role** from `theme-keys.json`: `SelectedBrush`, `FocusBrush`, `FocusHaloBrush`, `DangerBrush`, `InputBackgroundBrush`, `PrimaryButton*`, `ShellBackgroundBrush`, ...
3. **Shared control slot** (`<Control>[<State>]<Part>Brush`, e.g. `SliderTrackBrush`, `TopPanelItemCheckedBackgroundBrush`) only where the design gives that part its own token.
4. Two values for one role in different controls: the main control takes the role's key; the other reuses the key of the token it shares (Primo's pressed `Button` uses `HoverBrush`; its pressed `RepeatButton` uses `ButtonPressedBackgroundBrush`).
5. A role not in the vocabulary: add it to `theme-keys.json` first (key, type, group, one-line description), then use it. Never invent a key inside a theme.

**Naming** (new vocabulary entries): `<Control>[<Variant>][<State>]<Part><Type>` with Playnite's control names (`Button`, `ToggleButton`, `ComboBox`, `ListBox`, `GroupBox`, `SidebarItem`, `TopPanel`, `Tooltip`), never a design system's component names (ActionList, Card, AppBar, MenuPopover). General roles drop the control (`SelectedBrush`, `FocusBrush`); a plain fill drops the part (`SliderTrackBrush`, `MenuSeparatorBrush`). Spacing `<Control>Padding`; radii `ControlCornerRadius` (medium) and `CornerRadiusSmall`/`Large`/`XLarge`/`Full`; icons `Icon<Role>` drawn by `IconTemplate`; styles by what they style (`FocusVisual`, `BareTextBox`, `MainWindowButton`, `MainMenuButton`, `TopPanelSearchBox`, `SliderThumb`, `ScrollBarThumb`).

**Each theme keeps its own design.** Values, radii, spacing, shell, icon set and component shapes come from the design system's published spec, pinned to a version in its `AGENTS.md`; only names are shared. Map by role, not by color. Write the component spec in each file's header comment (component, tokens, sizes). A design system is more than colors: spacing (`Common.xaml`), shell, icons (`Media.xaml`), component shapes. Where WPF/Playnite can't follow the spec, list it under "Deviations" in `AGENTS.md`.

## ThemeModifier

Lacro59's ThemeModifier recolors a theme by **replacing Playnite's palette brushes** (`TextBrush`, `GlyphBrush`, `HoverBrush`, `ButtonBackgroundBrush`, `PopupBackgroundBrush`, ... 24 in all) in application resources, and edits the theme's own constants listed in `thememodifier.yaml`.

- Only `{DynamicResource <Brush>}` references follow a replaced brush. A `*Color` key, or a second key holding the same color, does not. Theme XAML reads **brushes only**; the build fails on a `Color` reference outside `Constants.xaml`. Gradient: fill with the brush, put the gradient in an `OpacityMask` (see any theme's indeterminate `ProgressBar`).
- Sanctioned exception: `HtmlTextView.HtmlForeground` and `LinkForeground` (game description) are Color-typed with a black default, so they read `TextColor`/`GlyphColor`; the check allows exactly those two attributes, and brush edits do not reach that text.
- Define palette and shared brushes as plain `SolidColorBrush` entries in the template. A brush pointing at another brush can't follow an edit.
- `build-theme.ps1` generates `thememodifier.yaml` next to `theme.yaml`: only defined keys opted in through `themeModifier` or `playnitePaletteConstants` in `theme-keys.json`. Expose the main surfaces, including existing sidebar and panel backgrounds, along with button fills and text and selection colors. The build and validator check that each defined opt-in appears in the manifest. Keep hover, pressed, and decorative colors in the theme. Ranged doubles such as `IconSize` remain editable. ThemeModifier 3.0.2 has 105 rows, and each heading after the first adds a spacer. When headings would exceed that limit, category names move into the labels. Edit descriptions in `theme-keys.json`.
- **Banner height ("Banner height (0 = off)")**: Defined as `GameBannerHeight` in `Common.xaml` (ranged `0,600` in `thememodifier.yaml`). ThemeModifier adjusts it dynamically: setting to `0` turns off/collapses the banner, decreasing shifts top elements closer to the top, and increasing shifts them down. The spacer MUST scale proportionally with `HeroArt.ActualHeight` via `{StaticResource MathConverter}` (`ConverterParameter='x * <DefaultSpacer> / <DefaultBanner>'`) and an `ActualHeight == 0` trigger; never bind spacer `Height` directly to `{DynamicResource GameBannerHeight}`.
- **Window background (issue #22)**: Playnite's Settings, Appearance, General, "Use game background image as window background" is the only way a theme shows game art behind the library; there is no theme or ThemeModifier option for it. `Views/Library.xaml`'s `PART_ImageBackground` shows the art at full strength: no `Opacity`, `Visibility` or `Effect` on it, no `OpacityMask` around it, no `ScrimBrush`/`ArtTintBrush` layer over it (Playnite's "Darken background image" and blur are the treatment; decor that doesn't depend on the art, such as a glow, grain or halftone, may stay). The image sits top-aligned in a `Grid` that sizes to it, with a `Rectangle` gradient from clear at 0.55 to the color behind the art at 1 (a collapsed `WindowArtSwatch` border bound to that brush), so the art's bottom edge fades out instead of ending in a hard line. A `{Settings ShowBackgroundImageOnWindow}` `DataTrigger` turns the top bar, the filter and explorer panels and the game pages (`PageRoot` or the page's root fill) `Transparent` and collapses `HeroArt` (`Visibility` `Collapsed`, not `Hidden`, so the spacer floor applies and `GameBannerHeight` has no effect). The art layer spans the whole window: the `Grid` that holds the swatch, the art and its decor goes before `TopPanel` with `Grid.RowSpan="2"`, takes the swatch brush as its Background while the setting is on, and reaches under the rail with a negative Margin set by `{Settings SidebarPosition}` (-44 left or right, -56 top or bottom); a theme whose rail sits outside a framed card (Shade) leaves the margin off. The top bar, the rail's solid fill (plus rail decor that needs it), Expander headers (`DefaultControls/Expander.xaml`, present in every theme) turn `Transparent` through the same `{Settings ShowBackgroundImageOnWindow}` trigger, and the scroll bar's track fill gets `x:Name="TrackFill"` and `Opacity` 0.4. `validate-extension.ps1` fails a solid rail, an opaque track fill and a missing Expander trigger. `DefaultControls/Slider.xaml`'s implicit style disables ThemeModifier's banner height slider meanwhile: ThemeModifier builds each constant row as a `Grid` whose first child is a label with `Tag` = the key, so a `MultiDataTrigger` on `{Binding Children[0].Tag, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=Grid}}` = `GameBannerHeight` and the setting = `True` sets `IsEnabled` False and `Opacity` 0.4; a second trigger does the same for `GameBannerDarken`. **Banner darkening**: `GameBannerDarken` (`Common.xaml`, default 0, ThemeModifier `0,1`) is the opacity of `<Rectangle Fill="{DynamicResource GameBannerTintBrush}" Opacity="{DynamicResource GameBannerDarken}" IsHitTestVisible="False" />` placed right after the banner's `PART_ImageBackground`, below the theme's fade to the page, followed by a floor layer: the same brush at `Opacity="0.5"` with `Tag="{DynamicResource GameBannerDarken}"` and a `DataTrigger` on `Tag` = 0 collapsing it, so any value above 0 starts at 50% (50% + 50% x value; low values were invisible otherwise). `GameBannerTintBrush` in `Constants.template.xaml` copies a theme color so the darker banner keeps the theme's cast: `ArtTintBrush` if the theme has one (a solid token, no alpha), else its darkest branded surface (`NormalBrush`, `SelectedBrush`, the window color); black only for black themes, paper for light ones. Art generators that write the overviews carry the same triggers. `validate-extension.ps1` checks the image, the banner collapse and the slider (`Test-WindowBackground`).
- **Metadata widths:** `GameDetailsPaneWidth` and `GridDetailsPaneWidth` both default to `300`. Their value is the usable metadata-content width, excluding the pane's horizontal padding and border. Apply the dynamic resource to the inner content, letting its outer frame size to content; a bare pane can use the width directly. Keep exterior column gaps separate. This matches Attache's 300px content in both views while preserving each theme's frame and padding. Test changing the width resource and padding, not just the default size.

## How Playnite loads a theme

Source: `source/Playnite/Themes.cs` (`ThemeManager.ApplyTheme`).
1. Only XAML whose relative path matches a file in Playnite's **Default** theme loads (`scripts/data/playnite-theme-api.json`); anything else is ignored.
2. Each theme file is first parsed **on its own**, with only Default resources present.
3. Files merge in pairs, `Default/A.xaml` then `Theme/A.xaml`, in API order: `Constants.xaml`, `Common.xaml`, `Media.xaml`, `DefaultControls/*`, `CustomControls/*`, `DerivedStyles/*`, `Views/*`. The later definition of a key wins.
4. `Toolbox pack` skips any `Fonts/` folder and any file identical to the Default copy.

## Top bar layout and search

- **Order and position:** every theme places `PART_TextMainSearch`, `PART_ToggleFilter`, then sorting together at the top left, after the main menu when it is shown there. Search never moves to the right or the center. Playnite inserts sorting after other tools into `PART_PanelMainItems`; moving that host alone does not put sorting beside filters. Keep the named host as a content-sized `Grid` with template-based column triggers that put `TopPanelSortSettingsTemplate` first. Preserve the other tools, plugin host, visibility preferences, progress controls and caption-button clearance.
- **Matching button heights:** explicitly size the main-item host, `TopPanelItem`, filter and notification plates to the theme's toolbar button height. Idle, hover, checked and active states keep that height. A centered auto-height Grid can shrink buttons to their glyphs; do not rely on the old StackPanel's stretching. Account for vertical margins in the outer bar and retain square icon buttons. Cold Seat's toolbar plates are **36px**, including the active filter and selected view.
- **Persistent magnifier:** Playnite hides `PART_SeachIcon` while focused or nonempty. Keep that required part as the placeholder and put the actual magnifier in an independent named `Glyph`. Empty/unfocused uses `TextBrushDarker`; focused or nonempty uses `GlyphBrush`. Focus and text change color only, never glyph visibility or input padding. Reserve the glyph's space while typing; decorative glyphs do not intercept clicks. Preserve explicit `ShowImage=False` behavior for fields that disable icons. Check every SearchBox template, including Ace and Materia's top-bar overrides and both MannCo templates.

Run `pwsh -STA -File tests/wpf/TopPanelLayoutRegressionTests.ps1` and `pwsh -STA -File tests/wpf/SearchGlyphRegressionTests.ps1`. Check toolbar items hidden by preferences, filter/selected-view active states, and empty → focus → typing → blur → clear without the magnifier disappearing. Update the HTML previews and render them with the same order and dimensions. For changes across themes, rebuild and redeploy every affected theme, preserve the active theme, restart a running Playnite once, and check its log for theme/XAML errors. A build drop alone does not update an installed theme.

## Hard rules (Playnite fails silently otherwise)

See the [shared theme guide](../../src/themes/AGENTS.md) for control behavior, including Statistics cards, ComboBox chevron spacing and game-page actions.

- Theme files are **overlays**: only restyled keys. Keep every `PART_*` and every part Playnite code dereferences (`SearchBox` needs `PART_SeachIcon`, `PART_TextInpuText`, `PART_ClearTextIcon`). Start from the Default file at the snapshot's tag; change visuals/layout, not behavior.
- Theme keys via `DynamicResource`. `StaticResource` only for Playnite keys or keys defined earlier in the same file.
- `StaticResource {x:Type ContextMenu}` in a later file resolves to the theme's own style (files merge one by one): use `BasedOn` that way instead of copying templates (SliderEx, GameMenu, GameGroupMenu, TrayContextMenu, TopPanelMenu).
- A Default style that references a sibling in its own file with `StaticResource`: redefine both (`Separator` + `MenuItem.SeparatorStyleKey`).
- `BaseStyle` already sets Opacity 0.5 when disabled; styles based on it must not add their own `IsEnabled` opacity trigger (0.25).
- Focus: buttons, toggles, checkboxes, tabs use a keyed `FocusVisualStyle` (`FocusVisual`; keyboard only). Text inputs draw focus on `IsKeyboardFocusWithin`. No `IsKeyboardFocused` border triggers on buttons (mouse clicks focus too).
- No hard-coded colors in theme XAML: add a token, a template line, and a vocabulary entry if the role is new.
- See [Control corner radii and shapes](../../src/themes/AGENTS.md#control-corner-radii-and-shapes) for radius rules and ThemeModifier’s 41px buttons.
- Only XAML attributes that exist on that element in Playnite's Default files. The build checks keys, placeholders and file paths, but never validates property names, so an unknown member (e.g. `CharacterCasing` on a `TextBlock` — it exists only on text inputs) passes build and validate, then crashes Playnite at startup. Never hand-write an attribute from memory: grep the Default snapshot for it on that element first.
- Icon resources Playnite copies (`Media.xaml` menu icons such as `AddGameIcon`, `PlayIcon`) are rebuilt from a `TextBlock`'s glyph and font, so a vector there is lost. To use the design system's icons, make each key a `sys:String` theme-relative PNG path (loaded through `ThemeFile`), rendered by `scripts/render-icons.ps1` from the theme's `icons.json`. Vector icons elsewhere are `Icon<Role>` geometries through `IconTemplate`.
- Game overview (`Views/DetailsViewGameOverview.xaml`, `Views/GridViewGameOverview.xaml`): every `PART_*` is optional (null-checked) but a name may appear once. All themes follow one skeleton (banner, header, then two columns: Steam screenshots + description + notes on the left, metadata pane on the right; screenshots never span over the metadata) and put **every** metadata field in one pane of six collapsing groups; layout, part names, triggers: `src/themes/AGENTS.md` -> Game page. Banner spacer scales proportionally with `HeroArt.ActualHeight` via `{StaticResource MathConverter}` (`ConverterParameter='x * <DefaultSpacer> / <DefaultBanner>'`), preserving default title/gradient alignment while moving top elements up/down dynamically when Banner height (0 = off) changes in ThemeModifier (never bind spacer directly to `{DynamicResource GameBannerHeight}`). List values are Buttons styled from code with `{StaticResource PropertyItemButton}`, so `DerivedStyles/PropertyItemButton.xaml` is the only hook. `HtmlTextView` takes `Color`s (see ThemeModifier).
- View switches (`Views/TopPanel.xaml`): `TopPanelSwitchDetailsViewTemplate`, `TopPanelSwitchGridViewTemplate`, `TopPanelSwitchListViewTemplate` are icons only (`IconDetailsView` / `IconGridView` / `IconListView` through `IconTemplate` at `IconSize`). No text word labels; the item's `Title` is the `TopPanelItem` tooltip.
- Slider: set `Track.Thumb` last (Track stacks parts in the order set). `ScrollContentPresenter` clips: anything drawn outside an item needs the gutter as the panel's margin.
- No `DropShadowEffect` on popups or tiles; popups keep a 1px edge (WPF popups are layered windows). Wrap masked art (`OpacityMask`) in an element with `BitmapCache`, except art that sits behind an animated control (next rule).
- **No `OpacityMask` on art behind anything that animates** (the game page banner behind an animated Play button, library art behind animated top bar items). While a control animates, WPF repaints only the patch behind it; on a scaled display (125%, 150%) a masked image re-rendered for that patch blends its edges with transparent black and leaves dark rectangles at the animated layers' bounds that stay after the hover. Pixel snapping, removing `BitmapCache` and ending the animations do not fix it. Fade such art with a plain gradient rectangle on top that goes from `#00000000` to the page color, read from the page's own brush so ThemeModifier still applies: name the page root (`x:Name="PageRoot" Background="{DynamicResource GameOverviewBackgroundBrush}"`) and bind the last stop to `{Binding Background.Color, ElementName=PageRoot}` (Cloudbank's game page).
- Tab pages inherit the selected `TabItem` foreground. Apply [header colours](../../src/themes/AGENTS.md#tab-colours) in `ControlTemplate.Triggers` so setters can target the header wrapper.
- Follow the [form field height rules](../../src/themes/AGENTS.md#form-field-height). A `DatePicker` overlay’s button must avoid `BasedOn="{StaticResource {x:Type ToggleButton}}"` because the file loads before the theme style and would resolve to WPF’s white system style.
- **Filter sidebar: 28px controls.** After scaffolding, size the preset dropdown, the Name search field, and all filter selectors to 28px high within the filter panel; make each save, rename and delete preset action button exactly 28×28px with zero padding, including its min/max sizing. Keep ordinary form controls at 32px. Give search and selector fields matching backgrounds and borders. Match dropdown indicators to the expanded details-view group indicator, positioned near the right edge. Keep the indicator and clear button transparent over the field background in every state, with separate space for the clear button, indicator and text so they never overlap. Preserve Playnite's named parts, dropdown, typing and clear behavior. Check empty and populated fields, hover, focus, long values and the preset row in Playnite. The scaffold's generic overlays do not implement this sidebar exception.
- **No storyboard through a transform from a `Style` trigger inside a template.** A path such as `(UIElement.RenderTransform).(ScaleTransform.ScaleY)` on an unnamed transform, started from an element's own `Style` `DataTrigger`, throws `Cannot animate '(0).(1)' on an immutable object instance` and takes Playnite down. It fires on the game page because the template is built with no game bound, so the `Game = null` trigger runs during template creation. `build-theme.ps1` misses it; `validate-extension.ps1` fails it (`Test-StyleTriggerComplexAnimation`). `TransformGroup` paths fail the same way with `'[Unknown]' property does not point to a DependencyObject`. Two fixes, both tested with the page built while no game is set: in a `Style`, animate plain properties only (`Opacity`, `Height`, `Width`, or `Margin` with `ThicknessAnimation`; for a scale, change `Height` in a fixed-size host so layout stops there); or, for anything needing a transform such as rotation, name the transform (`x:Name`, inside a `TransformGroup` name the child) and put the storyboard in the page's own `ControlTemplate.Triggers` under a `DataTrigger` on `{Binding Game, FallbackValue={x:Null}}`, with `Storyboard.TargetName` and a bare `Storyboard.TargetProperty` such as `Angle` (Medallion, Dropzone; hover animations in Play and `GridTileButton` work the same way).
- **Path data is not checked by the build.** A malformed `Data` string in an overview (`F1MM...` from pasting a geometry after an `F1M` prefix) only throws when the template is built, so it also crashes on opening game details. `validate-extension.ps1` fails it (`Test-PathDataSyntax`).
- No `--` inside XML comments, no `{{`/`}}` in template comments, no `Fonts/` folder (bundled fonts go in `src/Typography/`, see below).
- Keep `ThemeApiVersion` as low as the theme allows (2.9.0 = Playnite 10.45+). Major must match Playnite's.

## Bundled fonts (`src/Typography/`)

Playnite draws only the fonts Windows ships plus the ones a theme bundles; the HTML previews draw every name with a stand-in from `scripts/data/fonts.json`. So a stack led by a font Windows lacks (Eurostile, Rajdhani, Sora, Monofonto, a game's commercial face) looks one way in the screenshots and another in Playnite. Every such face is bundled:

- Put the TTFs in `src/Typography/` (`Toolbox pack` skips `Fonts/`, not `Typography/`) with the font's `OFL.txt`, and lead the stack with `./Typography/#<Family>`: `<FontFamily x:Key="HeadingFontFamily">./Typography/#Orbitron, {{text:font-heading|Segoe UI}}</FontFamily>`. Lead the matching `tokens.css` token and the previews' stacks with the same family name.
- Only open fonts (SIL OFL or similar) from `scripts/fonts/<font>/`. Never a commercial face; bundle its stand-in instead and say so in `info/NOTICE-<Dir>.txt` (font, author, license, the Typography folder).
- **Only the faces the theme uses.** Collect the `FontWeight`/`FontStyle` values on elements and styles that use that key (body fonts: every weight the theme sets anywhere) and copy just those, plus Regular when anything inherits the default weight. WPF synthesizes a missing bold; a missing Medium falls to the nearest face, so a weight the theme sets gets its own file. Examples: Relay ships Orbitron Regular only; Ayywi ships Unbounded Medium/SemiBold/Bold (no Regular: no heading inherits it) and Sora Regular/Medium/SemiBold/Bold.
- **Static files only.** WPF ignores variation axes and draws a variable font at its default instance. Use the static faces in `scripts/fonts/<font>/` or `scripts/fonts/<font>/static/`; to add a weight, cut an instance from the variable font with fontTools (`instantiateVariableFont`, then set name IDs 1/2/16/17, `usWeightClass` and `fsSelection` like the existing statics). A font whose license reserves its name (Orbitron: "with Reserved Font Name") can't be modified under that name: use the publisher's own static files (Orbitron's come unmodified from Google Fonts).
- **Latin and Cyrillic only.** A font that also carries other scripts (Rajdhani's Devanagari, Unbounded's and Cascadia's extra sets) is trimmed with `python scripts/subset-theme-fonts.py <files>` (keeps kerning, features, hinting and names); characters outside the set fall back to the next font in the stack, per character. Not for a font with a Reserved Font Name (Orbitron). Rajdhani went from 390 KB to 72 KB a weight.
- `HtmlTextView` (game descriptions) resolves only installed fonts, so a bundled body font falls back there to the next installed name in the stack.
- `validate-extension.ps1` runs `scripts/theme-fonts.mjs`: it fails a key whose preview face differs from the face Playnite resolves (first bundled or Windows font, `fonts.json` -> `windowsFonts`), a `./Typography/#Family` with no matching file, a bundled file nothing references, and a Typography folder without its license.

## Effects and motion (glows, sprites, animation)

- **Generate, don't hand-draw.** Glow, lightning, texture and other effect art comes from a deterministic generator script kept in the theme's `art/` (Python + Pillow/numpy, or Node), never pixels drawn by hand or copied from the source game. For substantial independent art work, the coordinator can delegate the generator using the current host’s tools. Use measured specs: sizes, alpha profiles and falloff distances sampled from reference captures (see `RESEARCH.md`), seamless-tile and 9-slice requirements, a fixed seed, and a contact sheet (`art/fx-sheet.png`) to review. Then check its diff and its output yourself (hash the sprites it should not have touched, zoom the new ones) and send it back with measured feedback when a sprite misses ("alpha > 0.3 spans rows 15 to 22, too flat"). Cloudbank's `art/sprites.py` is the worked example.
- **Sprites are white masks.** PNG with RGB 255 and the effect in alpha. XAML fills a `Rectangle` with a theme brush and uses the sprite as `OpacityMask` (`ImageBrush ImageSource="{ThemeFile 'Images/fx/<name>.png'}"`), so ThemeModifier recolors every glow; previews use the same file through CSS `-webkit-mask` / `-webkit-mask-box-image`. Never bake color into a sprite.
- **Scalable glows** are 9-slice: one sprite, a 3x3 `Grid` of `Rectangle`s each masked by an `ImageBrush` with an absolute `Viewbox` on its slice (Cloudbank `GlowFrameTemplate`). Fixed corner cells only, so a GroupBox stays content-sized. The host sits at a negative margin equal to the bloom width.
- **No GIFs.** WPF's `Image` shows only the first GIF frame, and a GIF bakes in its colors. Animate with storyboards instead:
  - Fades: `Trigger.EnterActions` / `ExitActions` with `DoubleAnimation` on `Opacity` and an easing function (`QuadraticEase`), never setters on the animated properties, so leaving mid-fade does not snap.
  - Looping motion (crawling arcs, scanlines, flowing energy): a sprite tiled on a wide `Rectangle` inside a `Canvas` (no layout clip) inside a `Grid ClipToBounds="True"`, moved by a named `TranslateTransform` exactly one tile per loop (`RepeatBehavior="Forever"`). Do not animate transforms inside brushes (they can be frozen).
  - Flicker: `DoubleAnimationUsingKeyFrames` with `LinearDoubleKeyFrame`s on a wrapper's `Opacity`.
  - Stop loops on exit by starting finite animations on the same properties (default `SnapshotAndReplace`) and give exit animations `FillBehavior="Stop"` so no clock outlives the fade.
  - Give pressed its own layer (a plate that fades in) instead of reusing the hover layer, or leaving while pressed strands the hover state.
  - Show layers with `Visibility` keyframes at the start of the fade-in and hide them at the end of the fade-out.
- Check motion in Playnite at a scaled display (125% or 150%), hover in and out several times and look for leftovers around the control; HTML previews show only the end state.

## Steam screenshots

`IsControlVisible` belongs to the plugin's shared settings. A Steam request can finish after another game is selected, so `True` alone must never reveal a section. Enclose the heading, `SteamScreenshots_SteamScreenshotsViewControl`, loading skeleton and any empty result in a separate `Grid x:Name="SteamScreenshotsGameScope"`. Its style defaults to `Collapsed`; two `DataTrigger`s set `Visible` for either `Game.PluginId = cb91dfc9-b977-43bf-8e70-55f46e410fab` or `Game.Source.Name = Steam`. The library ID covers renamed sources; the source name supports manually assigned Steam games. Null games and other sources match neither condition.

Keep eligibility on the parent, outside timed `Visibility` animations: a child clock cannot override a collapsed ancestor. A setter on the animated child is insufficient. Keep `FallbackValue=PluginUnavailable` on plugin bindings, and hide the whole section when the binding is unavailable. For a trigger timer, name `BeginStoryboard`, explicitly keyframe `Visible` at zero and `Collapsed` at the timeout, and remove it in `ExitActions`. For a per-game timer, bind `Tag` to `Game.Id` with `NotifyOnTargetUpdated=True` and restart it on `Binding.TargetUpdated`; put plugin/loading visibility on a separate parent so the clock cannot expose the skeleton over loaded content. ColdSeat demonstrates this and a localized `LOCNoItemsFound` result after the timeout. Do not show a screenshot empty state for non-Steam games or missing plugins.

Update any `art/` overview generator with the same gate and timer logic. Run `pwsh -STA -File tests/wpf/SteamScreenshotsRegressionTests.ps1` on Windows: it executes real WPF styles for both views of every registered theme. Required scenarios: initial non-Steam with stale plugin `True`; Steam loading then non-Steam before completion; late `True` while non-Steam is selected; no selection; switch details/grid and restore selection. For timed empty states also check timeout, a second Steam game restarting loading, successful loading, and plugin missing/disabled. In Playnite repeat Steam loading -> non-Steam and details/grid switching; static XAML validation alone does not prove the race is fixed.

## Interactive layer (required for new themes)

Recipes for the items listed in SKILL.md -> New theme -> Required interactive layer. Design each from the source; Cloudbank's files are the worked example of the mechanics, not of the look.

- **Play hover** (`DerivedStyles/PlayButton.xaml`): layers, bottom to top: a bloom (`GlowFrameTemplate` at -32, resting opacity 0.3 to 0.5), the plate, a hover plate in `PrimaryButtonHoverBackgroundBrush` at opacity 0, a pressed plate in `PrimaryButtonPressedBackgroundBrush` at opacity 0, the content, then any effect layer (arcs, sheen) at opacity 0 and `Visibility="Hidden"`. Enter: fade hover plate, bloom and effect in over about 0.2s; loops (crawl, flicker, shimmer) run only while hovered. Exit: fade back over about 0.35s, replace loops with finite glides, `FillBehavior="Stop"`. Press: fade the pressed plate in and out on its own trigger. No `Style.Triggers` setters on the background: the plates carry the color change.
- **Cover hover** (`DerivedStyles/GridViewItemStyle.xaml`): keep the selected look static (setters) and build hover from separate named layers (outline, bloom, marks) that animate. Draw everything inside the item's own spacing margin (`Margin="{Settings ItemSpacingMargin}"` grid, negative child margins no larger than the spacing). Set `Canvas.ZIndex` on hover so the bloom overlaps neighbours. A breathing loop goes on a wrapper's `Opacity`, not on the layer being faded.
- **Cover hover controls** (`DerivedStyles/GridViewItemTemplate.xaml`): start from Default, keep `PART_PanelHost`, `PART_ImageCover`, `PART_ButtonPlay`, `PART_ButtonInfo` and the empty-cover-name and darken-uninstalled triggers. Split the uninstalled darkening (static) from the hover shade (animated). Default sets the Play glyph from a `Content` character; set `Content` to an `Icon*` geometry instead (`IconDownload` for `IsInstalled = False`) and draw it through `IconTemplate`. Define `GridTileButton` in the same file, before use (`StaticResource`). Entrance: shade fades in, buttons rise about 10px and scale from about 0.86 to 1 with a small overshoot (`BackEase`), the second one 60ms later; exit reverses with `FillBehavior="Stop"` and hides the panel at the end with a `Visibility` keyframe. Cap the `Viewbox` (`MaxWidth`) so the buttons do not fill the whole cover. Outline draw-on effects use a fixed-size `Path` with `StrokeDashArray` equal to the perimeter in stroke widths and an animated `StrokeDashOffset`.
- **Empty game page** (`Views/DetailsViewGameOverview.xaml`, `Views/GridViewGameOverview.xaml`): the no-game condition is `{Binding Game, FallbackValue={x:Null}}` = `{x:Null}` (the fallback also covers a null DataContext). Hide the content panel with it, and show an empty-state `Grid` sized to `{Binding ViewportHeight, ElementName=PART_ScrollViewHost}` so it centres in the visible area. Text: `LOCErrorNoGameSelected` (themes cannot ship strings). Idle loops live in the element's own `Style` `DataTrigger` with `EnterActions` `BeginStoryboard x:Name="..."` and `ExitActions` `RemoveStoryboard`, so they stop when a game is selected. Those loops animate plain properties only; a loop that needs a `RenderTransform` belongs in the page's `ControlTemplate.Triggers` instead (Hard rules above: from a `Style` it crashes Playnite). Any decorative addition next to Playnite data (title suffix, badges) needs a trigger that hides it when that data is empty.
- **Details scroll-host visibility:** set `Visibility="Visible"` directly on the details `ScrollViewer` named `PART_ScrollViewHost`, especially when it uses `Style="{DynamicResource DetailsScrollViewer}"`. Playnite's inherited style collapses that host when its DataContext is null, hiding every child including the empty state. Keep the empty state and selected-game content as sibling panels inside the visible host, with opposite no-game visibility triggers. Verify null DataContext as well as a non-null model with `Game = null`; test selected game -> grid -> details with selection cleared, and selecting a game again. Apply the empty-state recipe to both overview files and preserve it in any generator that writes them.
- **Generated assets for realism:** backgrounds, light, glows, ornaments and textures come from generator scripts (Effects and motion above). Prefer white masks filled with theme brushes; full-color art is only for non-themeable illustration and ships with its generator. Busy textures behind lists and covers read as noise in a real library: keep those layers solid or gradient and put texture where content is sparse (panels, headers, empty states).
- **Verify in Playnite**, not only in previews: hover Play, covers and the cover buttons repeatedly at 125% and 150% scaling, deselect the game to see the empty state, and check ThemeModifier recolors every animated layer.

## Running game indicator

The game that is launching or running is highlighted wherever it appears: the details list row, the cover tile, the list view row and the game page's Play / context action cell (Playnite swaps Play for the context action, which reads RUNNING or LAUNCHING). It answers "which game am I playing?" at a glance: the whole item is framed and tinted in the running colour and breathes, with the theme's own motif on top. It must read clearly next to selection and hover without looking like either.

**Contract** (`validate-extension.ps1` `Test-RunningIndicator`, `pwsh -STA -File tests/wpf/RunningIndicatorRegressionTests.ps1 [-Keys <keys>]` on a build drop):

| Where | File | Binds to |
|-------|------|----------|
| Details list row | `DerivedStyles/DetailsViewItemStyle.xaml` (`DetailsViewItemStyle`) | `GamesCollectionViewEntry.IsRunning` / `IsLaunching` |
| Cover tile | `DerivedStyles/GridViewItemStyle.xaml` (`GridViewItemStyle`) | same |
| List view row | `DefaultControls/ListView.xaml` overlay holding only the implicit `ListViewItem` style (Playnite's list, headers and scroll viewer stay Default's; copy Default's row and add the indicator, Questlog's overlay is the shape) | same |
| Game page action cell | `DerivedStyles/PlayButton.xaml` defines `RunningActionIndicator` (a `Control` style); both overviews (and their generator) put `<Control Style="{DynamicResource RunningActionIndicator}" />` as the last child of the cell holding `PART_ButtonPlayAction` and `PART_ButtonContextAction` | `GameDetailsViewModel.IsRunning` / `IsLaunching` (the inherited DataContext) |

- One element named `RunningIndicator` per template, `IsHitTestVisible="False"`, `Visibility="Collapsed"` at rest, drawn with `{DynamicResource RunningIndicatorBrush}` (required shared key, editable in ThemeModifier). Inside it: **`RunningFrame`**, the running colour framing the whole item (`BorderBrush`, `Stroke` or a shape template's `Foreground` in `RunningIndicatorBrush`), and **`RunningWash`**, the running colour tinting the whole row or button background (required on rows and the action cell; optional on covers, where a band inside the edge replaces a tint over the art). Then the theme's motif.
- Two `DataTrigger`s in `ControlTemplate.Triggers`, after the hover and selected triggers: `{Binding IsLaunching}` and `{Binding IsRunning}` = `True`. Each sets `Visibility` `Visible` on `RunningIndicator`, starts a **named** `BeginStoryboard` in `EnterActions` and removes it with `RemoveStoryboard` in `ExitActions`. No clock may outlive the state, and rows are recycled by virtualization.
- **Visible on a selected or hovered item.** Put `RunningIndicator` **after** every layer the `IsSelected` / `IsMouseOver` triggers show or recolour (selection plate, outline, brackets, marks, pips) and before the content, and never touch it from those triggers. Order alone is not enough where selection draws an outline on the same edge: inset the running frame (covers: `Margin="4"` on `RunningIndicator`, so the selection keeps the outer edge and running the ring inside it; rows with an outline box: `Margin="3"` on `RunningFrame`). `validate-extension.ps1` fails a selection or hover layer drawn above the indicator (except one holding the content presenter). 27 cover templates and Holotape's rows hid the frame on selection before this rule.
- **Different from Play, selection and hover.** `RunningIndicatorBrush` is a different hue from `PrimaryButtonBackgroundBrush` (a lighter shade of Play's own colour does not count: yellow on an orange Play, a second green on a green Play) and from selection and hover. A status green, or a cold opposite of a warm accent. Never `GlyphBrush` / `SelectedBorderBrush` / `GridViewItemSelectedBorderBrush`, never text, never the filter's `DataChangeNotifBrush`.
- **Clear, not loud.** Rows (details and list view): `RunningWash` over the whole row at 0.14-0.2 and a **2px** `RunningFrame` with a 1px dark keyline inside (`<Border BorderBrush="{DynamicResource TextBrushDark}" BorderThickness="1" Opacity="0.7" />` as its child, same corner radius), in the row's own shape, plus the motif: the keyline vanishes on dark rows and outlines the frame on bright selected fills. Covers: a 2px `RunningFrame` inset 4px inside the cover in the cover's own shape, optionally an inner band (a thick border at about 0.18), plus the motif. The action cell: `RunningWash` at 0.18-0.25 and a 1px `RunningFrame` in the button's exact shape, plus the motif. Effective frame opacity stays at or above 0.35 at the bottom of the loop (`RunningIndicatorRegressionTests.ps1` checks it, and that the frame spans the item).
- **Follow the real shape, never square it off.** Read the template the item actually draws with and copy its geometry into `RunningWash` and `RunningFrame`: corner radius keys, chamfer and slant templates, Path data (`Stretch="Fill"`), arrowhead slabs (Inkbolt's selected row is `ArrowPlateTemplate`, so its running outline is a rectangle plus a 10px arrow tip), cut corners. A square overlay on a shaped item reads as the item changing shape.
- **The RUNNING button keeps Play's form.** Playnite hides Play and shows `PART_ButtonContextAction` (RUNNING, LAUNCHING, INSTALL) in the same cell. Both overviews (and their generators) give it `Style="{DynamicResource PlayButton}" Tag="ContextAction"`; the default `Button` style made it a different shape (Night City's double-cut plate and Inkbolt's arrow turned into squares). `PlayButton` names every Play-only cue (play glyph, prompt key cap) and collapses it in a `ControlTemplate` trigger on `Tag` = `ContextAction`. While `IsLaunching` or `IsRunning`, `PlayButton` fills that same plate with `RunningIndicatorBrush` (and a contrasting foreground when Play's ink would disappear on it). INSTALL stays Play's own colour. `RunningActionIndicator` copies Play's plate geometry (Night City: the `Chrome` path data; Inkbolt: `ArrowPlateTemplate` plus the arrow outline). The test renders the real cell (the `PlayButton` with "Running" under the overlay), so check `<key>-game-page-action.png`. `validate-extension.ps1` fails a context action without that style and tag.
- **Motion.** Recipe, kit and the per-theme levers: [running-motion.md](running-motion.md). Launching, on the button, the details row, the list row and the cover: a **progress sweep** in the item's own shape (a `RunningScan` band crossing, a foot line filling, the theme's mark reacting as the band lands), 1.4-2s per loop with a short rest. Running: an **idle pulse**, the frame breathing 0.7 to 1 and the mark idling, 2.4-4s per cycle; the Play plate pulses through a `ScrimBrush` layer over a solid running-colour plate (never a translucent plate), and the label stays opaque. No `DiscreteDoubleKeyFrame`, flicker or stepped keyframes in the launching storyboard; a launching storyboard that only pulses `RunningIndicator`'s opacity fails `validate-extension.ps1`. While running and hovered **on the button itself**, the label is `{DynamicResource LOCCancelLabel}` and the fill is a darker shade of the running colour (a scrim over the running plate), never the idle Play hover colour. Collapse the idle hover plate while launching or running.
- **Cancel follows the button, not the page.** One `MultiDataTrigger` on `{Binding IsRunning}` = True and `{Binding IsMouseOver, RelativeSource={RelativeSource Self}}` = True shows `CancelLabel` and hides `PlayContent`. `RelativeSource TemplatedParent` is the whole game page's pointer state (the button lives in the overview's `ControlTemplate`), so Cancel appeared with the pointer anywhere on the page; the validator rejects it. Cancel never shows while launching or at idle.
- **Every state text stays readable.** Label against plate at least 4.5:1 at the loop's worst frame (3:1 floor for large bold labels), measured by `tests/wpf/RunningMotionFrames.ps1`; the overlay above the label tints it at most 0.12; nothing but `CancelLabel` draws above the label.
- Animate `Opacity`, or a transform by `Storyboard.TargetName` inside the template. Never animate from a `Style.Triggers` storyboard through a sub-object (Hard rules), never start loops on `Loaded`.
- **List view rows use the theme's own selection**, not Default's `GlyphBrush` fill: `SelectedRectangle` takes `ListItemSelectedBrush` (or `SelectedBrush`) and the selected foreground `SelectedForegroundBrush` (or `TextBrush`), matching the details row. An accent-filled row hides any frame drawn on it.
- **Find the real shape before drawing.** The RUNNING button is `PART_ButtonContextAction`, usually on the theme's default `Button` style, not `PlayButton`: read `DefaultControls/Button.xaml`. Reuse its `CornerRadius` key, chamfer template (Uplink and Relay `ChamferTemplate`), skew (Backbeat, CallingCard rows) or sprite template (Hallowtide). Check the overlay `Control` shares the button's cell in both overviews; wrap Play and the context action in one `Grid` when they are StackPanel siblings (Uplink, Codex).
- **Content inside the fill border** blocks the layer order. Split a row whose `ContentPresenter` sits inside its selection plate into a plate `Border` plus a content `Border`, so the indicator can go between them (Ayywi, Blacklist, Chakram, Primo, Shade).
- **Generators.** When an `art/` script writes the overviews, add the line to the script too. If the script has drifted from hand edits (running it would rewrite unrelated lines), hand-add the line in both and note the drift; never regenerate over hand edits.
- **Look at it.** Run the test with `-RenderDir <scratch>` and read the PNGs (each item running and selected). Static checks passed while a shaped frame drew nothing, before the test loaded `Common.xaml`; only the renders showed the buried frames.
- Each theme records its mark in its `AGENTS.md` Components table (`Running game` row): motif, colour token, running and launching motion.

Tumbleweed is the worked example for the progress-sweep motion (see running-motion.md). Emberline is the example for frame, tint and shape handling: a frost tint and a 2px frost frame (ink keyline inside) around the row with a frost pilot light on its far edge (the red selection streak is on the near edge), a 2px frost frame inset 4px inside the cover over a soft frost band with frost light along its foot (the red selected frame keeps the outer edge), a frost-tinted, frost-framed action cell with the pilot light at its foot; breathing 0.65 to 1 over 3.2s while running, a smooth 0.8s pulse while launching.

## Game state indicators (any new state)

The running indicator is the template for any game state a theme marks on its items: installing or uninstalling (progress), favorite, hidden, custom game, recently added. Use it when the user wants a state "noticeable at a glance" across the library.

1. **Pick the binding.** Library items (`DetailsViewItemStyle`, `GridViewItemStyle`, list view `ListViewItem`) bind to `GamesCollectionViewEntry`: `IsRunning`, `IsLaunching`, `IsInstalling`, `IsUninstalling`, `IsInstalled`, `Favorite`, `Hidden`, `IsCustomGame` (all raise change notifications). The game page binds to `GameDetailsViewModel`: `IsRunning`, `IsLaunching`, `IsInstalling`, `IsUninstalling`, `IsInstalled`, `IsPlayAvailable`, `IsContextAvailable`, `IsInstallAvailable`; anything else through `Game.<Property>`. Check Playnite's source for the version in `scripts/data/playnite-theme-api.json` before relying on a property.
2. **Name it after the state.** A brush key `<State>IndicatorBrush` (and a `<State>ActionIndicator` style if the game page shows it) added to `scripts/data/theme-keys.json` with `required` and `themeModifier`; layers named `<State>Indicator`, `<State>Frame`, `<State>Wash`; storyboards `<State>Indicator<Phase>`. Never reuse `RunningIndicatorBrush` or the running layer for another state.
3. **Same anatomy as running.** Own layer above hover and selected, below content; frame and tint in the item's real shape; the theme's motif on top; `DataTrigger` with named `BeginStoryboard` and `RemoveStoryboard`; visible on selected and hovered items; a colour selection, hover, the filter mark and every other state indicator do not use.
4. **Match prominence to the state.** Live states the user is waiting on (running, launching, installing, uninstalling) frame and tint the whole item and move. Persistent attributes (favorite, hidden, custom) are a static mark only: a corner badge or glyph, no wash, no loop, so a library full of favorites stays calm. Progress states may fill along the frame or the foot instead of breathing.
5. **When states stack** (running and favorite, installing and selected), each keeps its own layer and position; live states draw above persistent ones. Decide and document the order in the recipe.
6. **Enforce it.** Clone `Test-RunningIndicator` in `validate-extension.ps1` and `tests/wpf/RunningIndicatorRegressionTests.ps1` for the new names (the test's fake game needs the new property), add the recipe as a section here, a row in the playnite-theme-dev skill table, a line in `new-theme.md`'s required interactive layer and `src/themes/AGENTS.md` Shell rules.
7. **Roll out** with the [theme patch workflow](theme-patch-workflow.md): prove it on one theme (validator, build, test, renders), write the recipe, then split the remaining themes by folder. Workers render their themes and look at the PNGs; the coordinator reviews the diffs (no lines lost from existing templates), composites every theme's renders into contact sheets, fixes what reads badly, runs `validate-themes.ps1`, `build-themes.ps1` and the test for all themes, then deploys each with `-NoRestart` and the active theme last with a restart. Each theme's `AGENTS.md` gets a `<State>` row.

## Motion by source type

Motion has a language per source. Pick the row, then measure the source (frame-step a capture, or read the motion tokens) before writing durations.

| Source | Play hover | Cover hover | Cover buttons | Empty page | Assets |
|--------|-----------|-------------|---------------|-----------|--------|
| Design system (Material, Fluent, shadcn, Chakra, Primer, ayywi) | Its own interactive states: state layer or elevation fade, ripple (Material), reveal highlight (Fluent), ring (shadcn, Chakra), 80-200 ms, its easing | Ring, elevation or scale 1.02, the system's focus/hover colour fading in; no ornament | Icon buttons of the system (round, rounded square, ghost) with its icon set, fade and 6-8 px rise | Its empty-state pattern: a quiet icon in a tinted circle or box, one line of text, no loops (or a slow 3 s fade) | None. Never generate glow sprites for a system that has no glow |
| Game menu with a signature effect (glow, sheen, ink, frost, rust, pixel) | The effect, animated in and out, looping only while hovered | Game's selection language animated (cursor, brackets, bevel flash, underline sweep, page-flip) | Buttons in the game's shapes and icon style | A game motif (empty slot, vault door, blank card, standby screen) with a slow idle | Generated from measured specs when the source has light or texture (reference.md -> Effects and motion); otherwise none |
| Pixel or retro game (Terraria, Minecraft, Fallout, Warcraft) | Frame swap: step the bevel or sprite in 2-3 steps (`DiscreteDoubleKeyFrame`), no smooth glows | Pixel-snapped outline pop or bounce | Pixel-art or bevelled square buttons | Sprite-style empty slot or terminal prompt blink | Pixel sprites from a generator at 1x, `RenderOptions.BitmapScalingMode="NearestNeighbor"` |

Always: fades, never snaps; loops only while visible; exit animations `FillBehavior="Stop"`; durations 120-350 ms unless the source is slower on purpose; no `DropShadowEffect`; no `OpacityMask` on art behind animated controls.

## Template placeholders (`Constants.template.xaml`)

| Placeholder | Result |
|-------------|--------|
| `{{name}}` | token color, alpha kept |
| `{{name@surface}}` / `{{name@surface@base}}` | flattened onto the surface (use for popup edges); a translucent last surface is an error |
| `{{name/NN}}` | token at NN% opacity |
| `{{a?b}}` | first token that exists |
| `{{name\|#hex}}` | fallback literal |
| `{{px:name[\|fallback]}}` | length in px (rem, px, var(), calc()) |
| `{{text:name\|fallback}}` | raw text (font names) |
| `{{TODO}}` | fails the build with "not mapped yet" |

Tokens are read from `:root`/`@theme`; selectors containing `dark` override them. Errors report file, line and key.

## Build checks

`build-theme.ps1` and `validate-extension.ps1` fail on: files outside Playnite's list, unrendered placeholders, malformed XML, unknown references, cross-file `StaticResource`, keys that are neither Playnite's nor in `theme-keys.json`, a vocabulary key with the wrong type, `Color` references outside `Constants.xaml`, a `Fonts/` folder. Missing **required** vocabulary keys: warning in `build-theme.ps1` (a theme in progress still deploys), error in `validate-extension.ps1`.

## Responsive game pages

Use the available game-page body and usable metadata widths in WPF device-independent pixels. Window width also includes the sidebar, game list, filters and other chrome.

| Layout | Breakpoint | Metadata |
|---|---|---|
| Wide | Body width is at least `preferred metadata width + theme column gap + 400` | One pane on the right at the preferred width |
| Medium | Below the wide breakpoint, with at least `560` of usable metadata width | Two columns in a full-width pane below screenshots, description and notes, with a `24` gap between columns |
| Narrow | Below the wide breakpoint, with less than `560` of usable metadata width | One column in a full-width pane below the content |

Keep the main column constrained by `MaxWidth`. The preferred metadata width comes from `GameDetailsPaneWidth` or `GridDetailsPaneWidth` inside the frame. Reset both `Width` to `NaN` and `MaxWidth` to `Infinity` in the stacked state, so the pane fills the body. Measure the metadata breakpoint inside the frame. Reserve the game page scrollbar gutter with `VerticalScrollBarVisibility="Visible"` so reflow cannot move the pane back across the breakpoint. The six existing `Meta*` groups wrap in order, and collapsed groups give up their slots. Keep each field's caption and value in the same group, and preserve the frame, group styles and first-row separator clipping.

For new themes, build both overview bodies with distinct main and metadata branches and the six groups under one metadata stack. Apply `scripts/game-page-breakpoints.mjs` to both files or call its helper in the generator. The generated XAML is standalone in each theme. Run `tests/wpf/GamePageBreakpointsRegressionTests.ps1` to check shrink and grow transitions, exact inner widths of 559/560/561, frame padding, preferred widths and hidden groups.

Preserve the header's minimum top gutter at short or zero banner heights and when `HeroArt` is collapsed. Empty grid views keep the top-left close action independent of banner height and selection. Also run the details and grid overview layout regressions, the side-panel close regression and the Steam screenshots selection regression.

Responsive boolean state can be null while WPF creates a ControlTemplate. In MathConverter, use an explicit comparison such as `z == true ? ... : ...` before a ternary; `z ? ... : ...` throws when z is null and can prevent Playnite from opening. Exercise deferred template creation and initial null bindings, not only a parsed standalone Grid.

The minimum banner gutter also applies to details view. Keep each view’s own side inset and existing header top margins when choosing the spacer floor, and preserve the default proportional banner expression. Verify tiny/zero/hidden banners and Ace’s compact metadata rows with `tests/wpf/DetailsViewLayoutRegressionTests.ps1`.
